Web Protection and Web Protection Profiles

Browse and edit a FortiWeb's Web Protection Profiles and every object of the FortiWeb Web Protection menu, tune signature policies, deep-clone a profile or save it as a template.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view protection.edit protection.apply operations.template_save
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile, and FortiWeb → Web Protection → <group> → <page> (URL /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>; signature editor /web-protection/<id>/signatures/<name>; the old /web-protection/<id> and /web-protection/<id>/m/<item> redirect)

What is it?#

The Web Protection pages are part of the FortiWeb device menu: the FortiWeb group of the sidebar, built from the GUI layout measured on the selected device's firmware build. They have the names and places of that FortiWeb's own GUI. Web Protection Profile (the WAF bundle a server policy binds) is under Policy; the protection areas — signatures, protocol constraints, access rules, input validation, cookie security, advanced protection, data loss prevention and the rest — are under Web Protection. Each page is drawn in FortiWeb's layout inside the SATOM frame, with SATOM's tools added.

What does it do?#

  • Web Protection Profile page — FortiWeb's Policy > Web Protection Profile list with its two tabs, Inline Protection Profile and Offline Protection Profile: Create New, Edit, Clone, Delete and Search, plus SATOM's Deep clone, Save as template, Hide default profiles and Factory catalog.
  • Protection area pages — one page per entry of FortiWeb's Web Protection menu, with FortiWeb's own tabs in FortiWeb's order and the same list columns the appliance shows. Each object opens in FortiWeb's dialog.
  • Signature editor — opened with the Signature editor button on Known Attacks → Signatures: the Signature Category table, a searchable Signature Details list over the cached signature catalog, per-signature Disable / Alert Only toggles, and the per-signature Exception tab.
  • Deep clone of an inline Web Protection Profile on the same device: SATOM walks the profile's sub-policies, reuses the ones that already exist and creates only the missing ones.
  • Save as template: stores the whole inline profile in the template library as a pending template for an administrator to approve, stamped with the appliance's running firmware build (see Template library).
  • Hide default profiles: hides FortiWeb's predefined profiles; a per-user toggle remembered between sessions.
  • Factory catalog button: opens the Factory catalog, the predefined ("default") profiles SATOM has stored per firmware build and REST API version. Use it to see a predefined profile's full tree, compare it between two builds, or save it as a template without picking an appliance. The button is shown to users with registry.view.

The Web Protection menu holds only the pages the device's build has. On FortiWeb 7.6.8 it is:

Group Pages
Known Attacks Signatures · Custom Signature
Advanced Protection Custom Policy · Padding Oracle Protection · CSRF Protection · HTTP Header Security · Man in the Browser Protection · URL Encryption · Link Cloaking · SQL/XSS Syntax Based Detection
Cookie Security (direct link)
Data Loss Prevention (direct link)
Input Validation Parameter Validation · Hidden Fields · File Security · Web Shell Detection · File Exception
Protocol HTTP · WebSocket · gRPC
Access URL Access · Allow Method · CORS Protection
ML Based Anomaly Detection (direct link)
Web Anti-Defacement (direct link)

FortiWeb 8.0.6 regroups the menu: it adds Client Side Security (Client-Side Protection, HTTP Header Security, CORS Protection, Subresource Integrity Check, Man in the Browser Protection, Cookie Security), Input Validation → File List and Protocol → MCP. Any other build shows what its own GUI has.

Requirements#

  • A registered FortiWeb, selected as the current device. With no device selected, the FortiWeb group holds only Server Policy, and opening /web-protection/ sends you to the Service Diagram page to pick one.
  • A GUI layout for the device's build, from the knowledge packs. Until one is imported, the Web Protection pages have no menu entry; the old pages at /web-protection/<id> still open from a bookmark.
  • For fast pages, a local copy of the device configuration. The lists are read from SATOM's local source of truth; use ⟳ to pull the live configuration first.
  • For signature names, descriptions and the Signature Details search: a cached signature catalog. An administrator creates it on the Signatures page.

Permissions#

Action What it needs
Open the profile list, the protection area pages, the signature editor, signature search protection.view
⟳ refresh, Deep clone (preview and apply) config_write, which any of protection.edit, protection.apply (or another *.edit / *.apply key) grants
Save, delete or clone objects, signature toggles, signature exceptions, category settings config_write (the dialogs' and the object editor's save, delete and clone calls)
Save as template operations.template_save

Without config_write, the ⟳ refresh, Clone, Delete and Deep clone buttons are hidden and Edit reads View. The signature editor still shows its toggles; their writes fail with an error message or an alert instead of a result. Save as template is shown only to holders of operations.template_save. The seeded Operator and Administrator profiles have all of these keys; Viewer has only the read keys, including protection.view.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: write buttons are hidden from users without config_write, and the hints for template-managed profiles and a missing signature catalog name the real menu entries, Administrator → Template Library and Administrator → Signatures.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the FortiWeb ADOM no longer draws SATOM's WAF group (Web Protection Profile, Web Protection and the protection areas). Web Protection Profile is at FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile and the protection areas under FortiWeb → Web Protection, as in the device's own GUI. The pages open at /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>; an old /web-protection/ address redirects to the page that draws the same objects. The signature editor opens from the Signature editor button on Known Attacks → Signatures, and the Classic view button is gone. Search Attack ID, Exceptions & Signature and WAF Artifacts are under Fleet → WAF.

How to use#

Open the Web Protection Profile list#

  1. Select a FortiWeb as the current device.
  2. In the sidebar open FortiWeb → Policy → Web Protection Profile.
  3. Use the Inline Protection Profile and Offline Protection Profile tabs.
  4. Type in Search to filter the rows, or tick Hide default profiles to show only custom ones. The toggle is saved to your user preferences.

The columns are FortiWeb's own. A Template badge (lock icon) marks a profile governed by an approved template.

Edit or create a profile#

  1. Select a row and click Edit (or double-click it), or click Create New.
  2. FortiWeb's Web Protection Profile dialog opens with the profile's sub-policies as reference selectors. The pencil beside a selector opens the selected sub-policy in a panel stacked over the dialog.
  3. Click Save, check Review the change, then click Apply to <device>.

A template-managed profile is read-only on the device: Edit reads View and Delete is unavailable. Change it in the Template Library; saving an approved template deploys it to every device it governs.

Browse a Web Protection page#

  1. In the sidebar open FortiWeb → Web Protection and pick a group and a page (for example Access → URL Access).
  2. Switch between FortiWeb's tabs at the top of the page (for example URL Access Policy, URL Access Rule and URL Access Parameter).
  3. Select a row, then use Edit, Clone (copies the object and its sub-table rows under a new name) or Delete.

Clone asks for a new name (default <name>-copy), shows a dry run (DRY-RUN: create "<new>" from "<name>") and writes only after you confirm. Delete asks Delete "<name>"?, shows the dry-run request and asks Apply this delete to the device now? before anything is removed.

Work in a signature policy#

  1. Open FortiWeb → Web Protection → Known Attacks → Signatures.
  2. Select the signature policy's row and click Signature editor.
  3. In Signature Category, click the pencil on a category to change Status, False Positive Mitigation (SQL Injection categories only), Action, Severity, Block Period (seconds) and Trigger Policy, then Save to device.
  4. In Signature Details, filter by class, sub-class and state (All signatures, Disabled only, Alert Only, With exceptions) or type in Search ID or description…. Results are paged 100 at a time.
  5. Per signature: - the power button disables or re-enables it in this policy; - the bell button sets or removes Alert Only (log, don't block); - the three-dots button opens Details / Exceptions.
  6. On the Exception tab of a signature click Create New, choose the Element Type and Operation, fill the fields the type needs, and click Save to device. Delete an entry with its bin button.

Every write asks for confirmation (This writes to the device.) and goes to the appliance immediately. After a write the list is re-read live from the device, because the box is now ahead of the local copy.

ℹ️Note

A predefined signature policy carries a Predefined badge: FortiWeb predefined signature policy — read-only; clone it to customize. To write exceptions for one Server Policy as tracked desired state instead, use Exceptions & Signature.

Deep-clone a profile#

  1. On the Inline Protection Profile tab, select the profile and click Deep clone.
  2. Enter the new name (default <name>-copy). SATOM reads the device and shows the dry run: the counts per status (for example create: 4, exists: 9; existing objects are reused) and the plan.
  3. Confirm Create on the device now?.
  4. The toast reads Deep clone created N object(s) and the page reloads with the new profile. If an object fails, the alert names each failed object and why.

Save a profile as a template#

  1. On the Inline Protection Profile tab, select the profile and click Save as template.
  2. Enter the template name (defaults to the profile name).
  3. The toast reads Saved "<name>" vN (pending approval). An administrator approves the template in the Template Library before it can be deployed.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
New name (deep clone) Name of the copied profile on the same device Yes WPP-Shop-Strict-copy
Template name Name of the pending template No (defaults to the source profile) WPP-Shop-Strict
Hide default profiles Per-user filter on the profile list No ticked
Signature search per_page Rows per page in Signature Details (10–400) No 100

Example#

🧪Example — Alert-only for one noisy signature

An operator sees signature 010000001 blocking legitimate checkout traffic on fweb-01. They open FortiWeb → Web Protection → Known Attacks → Signatures, select the signature policy used by the shop profile, click Signature editor, search for 010000001, and click the bell button. After confirming, the row shows Alert Only and FortiWeb logs the signature without blocking. To scope the exemption to one Server Policy instead, they would author it in Exceptions & Signature.

Result#

  • ⟳ (Pull live config from the device) pulls the device configuration into SATOM and shows Refreshed from <device>: <detail>.
  • A deep clone writes each missing object to the device, records a wpp.clone audit entry, then refreshes the local copy so the new profile is listed.
  • Save as template records a wpp.save_template audit entry and creates a pending template version.
  • Signature toggles, exceptions and category edits are applied to the device at once through the object editor.

Troubleshooting#

"Refresh failed: …"#

Possible causes - The appliance is unreachable or its credentials are wrong.

Solution 1. Check the device under Appliances. 2. Click ⟳ again.

Verification — the cache badge next to ⟳ shows the time of the refresh.

"No signature database cached — signature names/descriptions and the search need it"#

Possible causes - The signature catalog was never synced on this SATOM instance.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator to open Administrator → Signatures and run Sync now (see Signatures).

Verification — the Signature Details table lists signatures with descriptions.

"Nothing to create — "<name>" already exists on <device>"#

Possible causes - The new name is already used by a profile on the device.

Solution — run Deep clone again with a different name.

"Row id unknown — refresh the list (state may be stale)."#

Possible causes - The local copy does not hold the row id needed to remove a Disable or Alert Only entry.

Solution — click ⟳ on the Known Attacks → Signatures page, reopen the signature editor and retry.

The state badge on a signature policy says "unavailable"#

Possible causes - Neither the local copy nor the device returned the policy's sub-lists.

Solution — check the device is reachable, then click ⟳ on the Known Attacks → Signatures page.

Deep clone or Save as template is missing#

Possible causes - Deep clone needs config_write (for example protection.edit); Save as template needs operations.template_save. - Both act on inline profiles: the Offline Protection Profile tab does not show them.

Solution — switch to the Inline Protection Profile tab, or ask an administrator for the missing permission.

The Web Protection Profile page or a protection area is not in the menu#

Possible causes - No device is selected, or no GUI layout for the device's build has been imported yet: the FortiWeb group then holds only Server Policy. - The device's build has no such page in its own GUI.

Solution — select the device and check that the knowledge packs are up to date. A bookmark to the old page still opens it while no measured page draws that collection.

Advanced Internals
  • Lists are DB-first: they are served from the local source of truth and the device is contacted only on ⟳, after a write, or for FortiWeb's predefined entries, which are read live and marked live.
  • An old /web-protection/<id> or /web-protection/<id>/m/<item> address redirects to the measured page that draws the same collection; ?classic=1 keeps the old page. The signature editor at /web-protection/<id>/signatures/<name> is not redirected.
  • The signature policy editor reads its sub-lists (classes, disabled, alert-only, exceptions, sub-class disable, FPM disable) from the deep cache first and falls back to live reads. The page shows which source it used: DB cache, live device or unavailable.
  • A FortiWeb signature set holds at most 128 per-signature exception entries; the Exception tab states this limit.
  • Deep clone walks the profile's dependency tree; objects that exist are validated and reused, missing ones are created through the standard write path (sanitize, audit, change history).
  • Save as template stores the same deep snapshot as a template of kind web protection profile, with the note Cloned from <profile> on <device> (pending approval).
  • The old URL /web-protection/<id>/wpp/<name> redirects to the object editor.
